items.title: Section: Skilfully Cultivating One's Undertaking Opens — the Six Perfections Practised With Resolve, Illustrated First Through Giving

items.zh: 云何菩薩善修事業？謂諸菩薩，於六波羅蜜多決定修作、委悉修作、恒常修作、無罪修作。云何菩薩於施波羅蜜多決定修作？謂諸菩薩，現有種種可施財法，諸乞求者正現在前，有恩、無恩、有德、有失無有差別，要當施與。若人非人、若諸沙門、若婆羅門及餘世間，無有如法能令施心有所傾動。
items.en:
What is a bodhisattva's skilful cultivation of one's own undertaking? It means that bodhisattvas, with respect to the six perfections, cultivate them with resolute determination, cultivate them thoroughly and completely, cultivate them constantly, and cultivate them free of fault.
What is a bodhisattva's resolute cultivation of the perfection of giving? It means that bodhisattvas, presently possessing various forms of giving-worthy wealth or teaching, when a seeker genuinely appears before them, give without any distinction based on whether the recipient has shown gratitude or ingratitude, virtue or fault. No human or non-human, no renunciate or brahmin, and no other party in the world can, through any improper means, cause that giving mind to waver.
Commentary: Regarding "human or non-human" and the like — being born into the human realm, obtaining a human form, is called human. Being born into other realms — the hells, animals, the realm of hungry ghosts, and the eightfold host of gods, dragons, yakshas, asuras, garudas, kimnaras, and mahoragas — is called non-human. This is as explained in the Compendium of Establishing Illustrious Teaching. Being born human yet practising while aspiring towards becoming a demon-king or a Brahma is called a renunciate or a brahmin. A demon or a Brahma-heaven god themselves are called other parties in the world. This is as explained in the Compendium on Mutual Association.

items.title: Section: Thorough, Constant, and Faultless Giving — Withholding Nothing, Never Growing Weary, and Giving Only What Genuinely Benefits

items.zh: 云何菩薩於施波羅蜜多委悉修作？謂諸菩薩，現有種種可施財法，諸乞求者正現在前，一切施與，無有少物於諸有情而不能捨。於內身命尚能惠施，何況外物？云何菩薩於施波羅蜜多恒常修作？謂諸菩薩，於修惠施無有厭倦，恒常無間，於一切時，隨有所得即隨惠施，無所悋惜。云何菩薩於施波羅蜜多無罪修作？謂諸菩薩遠離如前施品所說諸雜染施，修行所餘無雜染施。
items.en:
What is a bodhisattva's thorough cultivation of the perfection of giving? It means that bodhisattvas, presently possessing various forms of giving-worthy wealth or teaching, when a seeker appears, give everything, with no small thing at all that cannot be relinquished to sentient beings. Since a bodhisattva can give even their own inner body and life, how much more so external things.
What is a bodhisattva's constant cultivation of the perfection of giving? It means that bodhisattvas, in cultivating giving, are never weary, sustaining it constantly and without interruption, giving away at every moment whatever has just been received, without any stinginess.
What is a bodhisattva's faultless cultivation of the perfection of giving? It means that bodhisattvas stay far from the various tainted forms of giving already explained in the earlier chapter on the perfection of giving, cultivating instead the remaining, untainted giving.
Commentary: Regarding "staying far from the various tainted forms of giving already explained in the earlier chapter on the perfection of giving" — the chapter on the perfection of giving explains: if a bodhisattva knows that various internal or external items of giving would, for a given being, bring only ease without genuine benefit, or would bring neither ease nor benefit, that bodhisattva does not give them. If a bodhisattva knows that various internal or external items of giving would, for a given being, certainly bring benefit though not necessarily ease, or would certainly bring both benefit and ease, that bodhisattva does give them. This is, in brief, what should and should not be given. What is meant here by tainted and untainted giving should be understood accordingly.

items.title: Section: The Same Fourfold Structure Extends to All Six Perfections — Closing Skilfully Cultivating One's Undertaking, the First of the Four Dharmas, in Full

items.zh: 如是菩薩於施波羅蜜多能善修作。如於施波羅蜜多能善修作，如是於戒、忍、精進、靜慮、慧波羅蜜多，如其所應，當知亦爾。是名菩薩由四行相，於其六種波羅蜜多決定修作、委悉修作、恒常修作、無罪修作。
items.en:
In this way, a bodhisattva is able to skilfully cultivate the perfection of giving.
Just as one is able to skilfully cultivate the perfection of giving, one should understand that moral discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom are, as befits each, likewise cultivated in the same way.
This is called a bodhisattva's cultivation, through these four modes, of resolute cultivation, thorough cultivation, constant cultivation, and faultless cultivation with respect to the six perfections.

items.title: Section: Skilful Means Opens — Ten Kinds, From Dispelling Hostility Towards the Teaching to Mastery of All Three Vehicles

items.zh: 云何菩薩方便善巧？當知如是方便善巧，略有十種。何等為十？一者、憎背聖教有情，除其恚惱方便善巧；二者、處中有情，令其趣入方便善巧；三者、已趣入者，令其成熟方便善巧；四者、已成熟者，令得解脫方便善巧；五者、於諸世間一切異論方便善巧；六者、於諸菩薩淨戒律儀受持、毀犯，能正觀察方便善巧；七者、於諸正願方便善巧；八者、於聲聞乘方便善巧；九者、於獨覺乘方便善巧；十者、於其大乘方便善巧。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's skilful means? One should understand that this skilful means comprises, in brief, ten kinds. What are these ten? First, skilful means for dispelling the hostility of beings who resent and turn against the noble teaching. Second, skilful means for causing neutral beings to enter the teaching. Third, skilful means for maturing those who have already entered. Fourth, skilful means for bringing those already matured to liberation. Fifth, skilful means regarding every worldly discipline outside the teaching. Sixth, skilful means for correctly discerning the keeping and violation of the pure precept-discipline bodhisattvas receive and uphold. Seventh, skilful means regarding correct vows. Eighth, skilful means regarding the disciple's vehicle. Ninth, skilful means regarding the solitary awakener's vehicle. Tenth, skilful means regarding the great vehicle.

items.title: Section: All Ten Kinds of Skilful Means Cross-Referenced to Their Own Fuller Treatment Elsewhere in the Treatise

items.zh: 如是一切方便善巧，如前即此菩薩地中，隨彼彼處已廣分別，如應當知。
items.en:
All of this skilful means, exactly as already explained at its appropriate place elsewhere within this very Bodhisattva Stage, has been explained at length; it should be understood accordingly.
Commentary: Regarding "explained at length at its appropriate place elsewhere, understood accordingly" — among these, the first four kinds of skilful means correspond to the six kinds of skilful means for maturing beings already explained in the chapter on the factors of awakening. That same chapter also explains skilfully knowing the various treatises — this is the fifth skilful means here. The chapter on moral discipline explains the bodhisattva's own perfection of moral discipline — this is the sixth skilful means here. The chapter on the factors of awakening also explains a bodhisattva's own cultivation of correct vows — this is the seventh skilful means here. The chapter on the qualities of a bodhisattva explains establishing through vehicles — these are the final three kinds of skilful means here.

items.title: Section: Five Functions of Skilful Means Open — Establishing Beings in Their Own Good, Subduing Rival Views, and Keeping the Precepts Radiantly Pure

items.zh: 如是十種菩薩所有方便善巧，能作五事。謂由前四種方便善巧，令諸菩薩能正安立所化有情於自義利。由於世間一切異論方便善巧，令諸菩薩善能摧伏一切異論。由於菩薩淨戒律儀受持、毀犯，能正觀察方便善巧，令諸菩薩不犯所犯，犯已速疾如法悔除，於善清淨菩薩所受淨戒律儀，能善修瑩。
items.en:
These ten kinds of skilful means a bodhisattva possesses are able to perform five functions. First, correctly establishing the beings being taught in their own genuine good. Second, being able to overcome every rival doctrine. Third, enabling bodhisattvas not to commit what should not be committed, and, having committed it, swiftly and properly confessing and removing it, so that the pure precept-discipline received is skilfully kept polished bright. Fourth, enabling bodhisattvas to bring to complete fulfilment every cherished aim in the future. Fifth, enabling bodhisattvas, according to each being's own lineage and resolute understanding, to speak a fitting teaching, speaking in accordance with correct principle.
This means that, through the first four kinds of skilful means, bodhisattvas are able to correctly establish the beings being taught in their own genuine good.
Through skilful means regarding every worldly discipline, bodhisattvas are able to skilfully overcome every rival doctrine.
Through skilful means for correctly discerning the keeping and violation of the pure precept-discipline bodhisattvas receive, bodhisattvas do not commit what should not be committed, and, having committed it, swiftly and properly confess and remove it, keeping the pure precept-discipline received skilfully polished bright.
Commentary: Regarding "polished bright" and the like — a wholesome, pure aspiration is called genuinely pure. This refers to a bodhisattva's own capacity, an intrinsic quality that makes one fit to receive the precepts, through which one is able to receive the pure precept-discipline bodhisattvas receive. Here it is explained that, through that skilful means, the precepts are kept pure — this is called being skilfully polished bright.

items.title: Section: The Fourth and Fifth Functions Close — Fulfilling Every Cherished Future Aim, and Teaching Each Being According to Its Own Lineage, Closing Skilful Means Entirely

items.zh: 由於正願方便善巧，令諸菩薩能證當來一切所愛事義圓滿。由於三乘方便善巧，令諸菩薩於諸有情，隨其種性、根及勝解，說相稱法、說順正理。是名十種方便善巧，令諸菩薩能作五事。由此五事，能令菩薩現法當來一切事義皆得究竟。
items.en:
Through skilful means regarding correct vows, bodhisattvas are able to realise the complete fulfilment of every cherished aim in the future.
Through skilful means regarding the three vehicles, bodhisattvas, according to each being's own lineage, faculty, and resolute understanding, are able to speak a fitting teaching, speaking in accordance with correct principle.
These ten kinds of skilful means, then, enable bodhisattvas to perform these five functions. Through these five functions, bodhisattvas bring every undertaking, present and future alike, to its own ultimate completion.

items.title: Section: Benefiting Others Through the Four Means of Gathering — Three Classes of Beings, Closing the Third Dharma in Full

items.zh: 云何菩薩饒益於他？謂諸菩薩依四攝事，即布施、愛語、利行、同事，能與一分有情利益，能與一分有情安樂，能與一分所化有情利益安樂，是名略說菩薩所有饒益於他。廣說如前自他利品，應知其相。
items.en:
How does a bodhisattva benefit others? It means that bodhisattvas, relying on the four means of gathering — namely, giving, loving speech, beneficial conduct, and cooperation — are able to give benefit to a portion of beings, are able to give ease to a portion of beings, and are able to give benefit and ease together to a portion of the beings being taught. This is, in brief, called a bodhisattva's benefiting of others. Its fuller explanation is exactly as given earlier in the Chapter on Benefiting Self and Others; one should understand its characteristics accordingly.
Commentary: Regarding "able to give benefit to a portion of beings" and the like — here, the first two kinds of beings are described only as "a portion," without the qualifier "being taught," and one should understand that this refers to beings not abiding in any lineage, distinct from the "portion of beings being taught" mentioned afterwards. The boundless realm of what is to be tamed, already explained earlier, one should understand, is what "beings being taught" refers to here. Bestowing wholesome teaching upon all such beings is called giving benefit; bestowing material aid is called giving ease.

items.title: Section: Undistorted Dedication — Every Accumulated Merit Directed Solely Towards Awakening, Never Towards Worldly Reward, Closing All Four Dharmas in Full

items.zh: 云何菩薩無倒迴向？謂諸菩薩三門積集所有善根，即善修事業、方便善巧、饒益於他。去來今世一切攝取，以淳一味妙淨信心，迴求無上正等菩提。終不用此所集善根，希求世間餘果異熟，唯除無上正等菩提。
items.en:
What is a bodhisattva's undistorted dedication? It means that bodhisattvas, having accumulated all wholesome roots through three doors — namely, skilfully cultivating one's own undertaking, skilful means, and benefiting others — take up all of these wholesome roots across the past, future, and present, and, with a single, wholehearted, sincere, pure faith, dedicate and turn them towards unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening. Never do bodhisattvas use these accumulated wholesome roots to seek any other worldly resultant fruit — except unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening.
Commentary: Regarding "across the past, future, and present, take up all" — this means that, at every single time without exception, one gathers in, increases, and habituates these same wholesome roots until they become one's own nature.

blocks.text: The four dharmas that bring householder and renunciant bodhisattvas swiftly to awakening, explained one by one.
"Cultivating the six perfections resolutely, thoroughly, constantly, and faultlessly." Venerable Miào Jìng: "thoroughly" means in great detail and depth.

Venerable Miào Jìng: if they take the money and do evil, harming beings, then there is fault. Master Cháng Bǎi: all giving takes beings' benefit as its premise; whether their life becomes comfortable is secondary.
"First, skilful means for dispelling the hostility of beings who resent the noble teaching." Venerable Miào Jìng: first remove their inner hatred towards the Dharma.

Venerable Miào Jìng: one should study worldly rival doctrines after attaining acceptance of non-arising, not at the beginning. Master Cháng Bǎi: mastering logic, medicine, linguistics, and crafts, one can overcome rival views. On "polishing" the precepts: 瑩 means purity; purifying the mind in the very instant a thought stirs. Venerable Miào Jìng: "not easy".

Venerable Miào Jìng: lineage is what you have before practising; faculty is the merit cultivated after you come to believe. Master Cháng Bǎi: śrāvaka-lineage practitioners have special conviction towards renunciation, bodhisattva-lineage ones towards bodhicitta.
"With single, pure faith they dedicate them to supreme awakening, never seeking any other worldly fruit." Venerable Miào Jìng: "I seek not human wealth but supreme awakening": that is "turning" (迴向).
Venerable Miào Jìng's advice on rival doctrines is realistic: learn your own path deeply first. Debate comes after realisation, not before.

quiz.q: Skilfully cultivating one's undertaking means practising the six perfections in which four ways?
quiz.why: "Cultivating the six perfections resolutely, thoroughly, constantly, and faultlessly." Venerable Miào Jìng: "thoroughly" means in great detail and depth.

quiz.q: On "faultless" giving, what kind of giving do the lectures say is faulty?
options: Miào Jìng: if they use the money to do harm, it's faulty — giving that corrupts is tainted; Cháng Bǎi: all giving puts beings' true benefit first, comfort second
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: if they take the money and do evil, harming beings, then there is fault. Master Cháng Bǎi: all giving takes beings' benefit as its premise; whether their life becomes comfortable is secondary.

quiz.q: What is the first of the ten kinds of skilful means?
options: dispelling the hostility of those who resent the teaching
quiz.why: "First, skilful means for dispelling the hostility of beings who resent the noble teaching." Venerable Miào Jìng: first remove their inner hatred towards the dharma.

quiz.q: Among the five functions is "overcoming rival doctrines." When does Venerable Miào Jìng say one should study them?
options: after attaining non-arising acceptance, not at the outset
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: one should study worldly rival doctrines after attaining acceptance of non-arising, not at the beginning. Master Cháng Bǎi: mastering logic, medicine, linguistics, and crafts, one can skilfully overcome all rival views.

quiz.q: "Skilfully keeping the precepts polished bright (修瑩)." How do the lectures explain it?
options: both: 瑩 means purity — making the mind pure in the very instant a thought arises
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 瑩 means purity — making the mind pure; in the instant a thought stirs, purifying the mind is "skilfully polishing." Venerable Miào Jìng: purifying it from the very first instant — not easy.

quiz.q: In "according to lineage, faculty, and conviction," how does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish lineage and faculty?
options: lineage is present before any practice; faculty is merit cultivated after taking up the dharma
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: lineage is what you have before practising; faculty is the merit cultivated after you come to believe in the dharma. Master Cháng Bǎi: śrāvaka-lineage practitioners have special conviction towards renunciation, bodhisattva-lineage ones towards bodhicitta.

quiz.q: Undistorted dedication turns roots from three doors towards what, and never towards what?
options: supreme awakening; never any other worldly fruit
quiz.why: "With single, pure faith they dedicate them to supreme awakening, never seeking any other worldly fruit." Venerable Miào Jìng: "I seek not human wealth but supreme awakening" — that's "turning."
